newsitem.title: UK: MAM shares slip as bid speculation fades.
newsitem.headline: MAM shares slip as bid speculation fades.

text.p: Shares in Mercury Asset Management Plc came under pressure on Thursday after the market interpreted the fund manager's move to raise a standby loan as a deterrent to predators. The stock was 29.5 pence lower at 1339 by 1011 GMT.

MAM shares had risen steeply in the past few weeks on speculation the firm might be swallowed up by a larger group. But market makers said news of the 250 million stg loan, which MAM will not need to use immediately, was seen as a signal that the firm was determined to stay independent.
"People interpreted this as MAM trying to make themselves bid proof," said one dealer.
Market makers said comments in the Financial Times' Lex Column, which suggested the shares looked expensive now a takeover seemed unlikely, had also hit the stock.

The newspaper said MAM had put the loan in place as a contingency to plug any hole which might appear in funds it manages. This would help it cope with the sort of crisis that affected its rival Morgan Grenfell Asset Management in September, the paper said.
